parsed.explanation: Combined federal and state regimes impose binary documents, birth-sex facilities in schools/government settings, secondary entry screening with possible permanent fraud ineligibility, and documented custody harms including hormone withdrawal and, in immigration custody, forced labour and sexual abuse. No capital punishment or routine imprisonment for trans expression is documented, and courts have enjoined some orders, but remedies are slow, state hate-crime/discrimination protection is absent, and hostile official framing is extensive. Outing therefore risks exclusion, humiliation, detention and loss of future entry, though not the organised lethal targeting of lower anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary sex rule; new X/mismatched passport processing stopped Feb 2025, existing X valid until expiry; document discrepancy triggers refusal, and suspected wilful misrepresentation may support permanent fraud ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, and limited waivers exist; Supreme Court allowed restrictions Nov 2025 while litigation continues.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry discrepancy can escalate to investigation, refusal and future ineligibility, interacting with state document limits and not cured by local protections.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policy from 2026 adopts hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No visitor-specific custody protocol or independent oversight remedy is described; bureau stopped reporting number of trans prisoners from 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention for fraud, trespass or immigration grounds could lead to birth-sex placement or the documented abusive practices, with consular help not documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal binary definition bars congruent government single-sex facilities; division restricts trans K-12 school bathrooms from 2023, extended 2025, and Act 619 creates a conditional misdemeanour where a minor is present and sexual intent is proved.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Act 619 requires intent and additional circumstances; enforcement record not documented. Federal bans are contested and several orders enjoined, but operative scope uncertain.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal government-building rules plus state school rules create overlapping birth-sex exposure across journey stages; state title does not override federal facilities or entry screening.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for under-18s, currently re-allowed after Aug 2025 appeals reversal with litigation continuing; practitioners may cite religious beliefs to deny LGBT healthcare.
care_services.protection: Emergency/general care protection for visitors not documented; litigation has sometimes enjoined care bans for irreparable harm, but outcome unresolved.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor or adult needing continuity may face denial, while document mismatch and religious-refusal permission compound access barriers.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Orders direct investigation/prosecution over school gender-ideology and social transition, rename sex binary, and 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender; cash-reward guidance uses radical gender ideology framing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders blocked/enjoined; federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity since 2009, but division has no state hate-crime enhancement and no state gender-identity discrimination law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing increases police discretion at borders, schools and facilities despite partial judicial checks.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor care ban, school bathroom restriction, ban on trans girls/women in K-12/collegiate sports, and potential investigation of teachers facilitating preferred names/pronouns affect a travelling minor and guardian.
minors_guardians.protection: Care-ban enforceability is expressly not fully resolved and litigation continues; no documented visitor-specific exemption for minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family travel links school, sport, bathroom and healthcare exposures; a minor's care or school enrolment can trigger guardian and provider liability concerns.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No visitor-specific pattern of street violence is documented. Public support is high for birth-sex documents and sports restrictions, and national guidance notes safety varies and advises checking violence reports.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime coverage exists, but division excludes gender identity from state hate-crime law and civil intimidation remedy covers only race, religion or ethnicity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Hostile climate plus absent state recourse may reduce practical police protection if harassment occurs, but frequency for visitors is not_documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit and challenges to executive orders unresolved; state remedies slow/partial, local ordinances unenforced for broader protections, and several operative scopes, including Act 619 enforcement and care-ban status, remain uncertain.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined some measures, federal employment and hate-crime rulings remain, and legal-aid guidance exists; compensation or prompt release for visitors not documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper protections coexist with efficient hostile federal/state enforcement, so rule of law does not neutralise documented facility, document and custody exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in routine identity checks, discretionary detention, humiliation and weak practical remedy. This case is higher because imprisonment/execution is not routine, fraud ineligibility is conditional, and some federal orders are enjoined, whereas 0.35-B shows systematic police stops and ineffective courts.

Closest: universal document-linked exposure, detention/humiliation and denial of services, with custody unlikely for visitors and slow remedies. This case adds explicit federal facility exclusion, possible permanent entry bar, and harsher documented custody practices, placing it near this level.

Lower than 0.55-C because ward/document-based denial there is partial, emergency care moves faster, and advocate/ethics remedies work. Here birth-sex facilities, minor-care prohibition, hostile threat-framing and documented custody abuse are more extensive, despite no credible execution pathway.

Materially lower: 0.65-B has a working ombudsperson who reverses care refusal within hours. No equivalent prompt, documented visitor remedy is shown here; instead litigation is unresolved and state protection is absent.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is cumulative: binary federal documents and entry screening can cause refusal or future ineligibility; federal and state facility rules then force birth-sex access in schools and many government spaces; and any detention exposes the traveller to documented hormone withdrawal and abusive custody. Courts, federal hate-crime law and enjoined orders prevent a lower severe-risk rating, but they do not provide a prompt visitor remedy or cancel these universal, state-imposed exposures. For a minor, care, school and sport restrictions add a further layer.
